topic.title: Choosing a Project Structure for Translation
topic.shortdesc: How to organize source and translated content into folders and branches, and how the agent decides which layout to use.

section.title: The Default Project Layout
section.p: By default, organizes source and translated content as a folder pair per language, all on the same branch:

ul.li: The English source content lives under an en/ folder.
Each target language lives under its own top-level folder, named after the language tag (for example fr-FR/ or de-DE/).
Inside each language folder, files are laid out at the same relative paths as their English counterparts (for example en/topics/install.dita and fr-FR/topics/install.dita).

section.p: This is the layout the agent assumes when it sets up a project on the first translation job, and the one described throughout this documentation unless stated otherwise.

section.title: How the Agent Determines the Layout
section.p: When a translation job starts, the agent decides which layout to use in three steps:

ol.li: If a custom layout is documented in agent-instructions.md, the agent follows it.

Otherwise, the agent tries to detect the layout from the existing content. If you use a non-default layout, document it in agent-instructions.md so the agent follows it reliably instead of having to infer it every time.
If no layout is detected, the agent uses the default layout described above.

section.title: Choosing a Custom Layout
section.p: If the default layout does not fit your project, you can use a different one, as long as it respects these constraints:

ul.li: For compatibility with other tools, keep all DITA resources in subfolders of the folder that contains the DITA map.

Give each source file the same relative location in every target language as it has in the source language. Otherwise, links have to be updated during translation which is an error-prone process. For example identifying french files by an -fr suffix is not recommended.

Store the source and target languages on the same branch. For example, to keep an editing branch that contains only English files, create a parallel branch that holds both the English source and all the translations in the default per-language layout, and merge the editing branch into it before each translation job.

section.p: Document any non-default layout in detail in agent-instructions.md so the agent follows it. See Customizing the Translation Behavior.
